title: Garren Holt and the Old Paths

paragraphs.text: Garren Holt keeps his back near a wall and his eyes on every exit from the village green. He looks like a man who learned long ago that silence is safer than being understood badly.

When the old paths or the shrine come up, his expression goes colder rather than guilty. "Stay off the old paths if you value your skin," he says. "They have been busier than they have any right to be."
Garren has useful route knowledge, but he is measuring whether you came for a witness or an easy culprit. Respect may get you farther than accusation.

passive_social_insight.label: Garren's hostility is defensive, not proof

on_success.text: Garren is watching for accusation, not hiding triumph. His warning has the hard edge of someone who believes the old paths are dangerous and does not want his caution turned into gossip.

relationship_writes.reason: The player reads Garren as defensive rather than confirmed guilty.

clarifying_questions.label: What did you actually see on the old paths?

result.text: "Too many boots for a path people claim to avoid," Garren says. "Not villagers out for firewood. Not hunters moving careful. People moving like something had already decided where they would end up."
result.summary: Garren saw unusual traffic on the old paths before the attacks worsened.

result.text: "Because frightened people walk toward answers that feel like traps," he says. "And because I know how fast the old paths stop being old when enough fools decide to test them."
result.summary: Garren warns people away because the old paths have become dangerous and crowded with bad decisions.

relationship_writes.reason: Garren doubles down on caution rather than route detail.

result.text: Garren looks past you toward the old trees. "Tracks started bending that way. Not all at once. Enough that a man who knows the ground starts asking why everyone else forgot how to see it."
result.summary: Traffic on the old paths began bending toward the shrine before the road trouble worsened.

knowledge_grants.title: Garren's Observation
knowledge_grants.summary: Garren saw traffic near the shrine increase before the attacks worsened, as if people were being drawn there.

relationship_writes.reason: Specific route questions move Garren away from defensive posture.

result.text: "People who know better. People who do not. People who think being desperate makes them quiet." His mouth twists. "That is not a list of names. It is a warning."
result.summary: Garren cannot name every traveler on the old paths, but he knows the traffic is broader than ordinary hunting or woodcutting.

relationship_writes.reason: Asking for names increases pressure without yielding a culprit.

clarifying_questions.label: Why does being suspected make this more dangerous?

result.text: "Because once a village decides a man is the shape of its fear, it stops looking at the ground," Garren says. "And the ground is where the truth keeps leaving marks."
result.summary: Garren worries that village suspicion is making people miss useful evidence.

knowledge_grants.title: Village Suspicion
knowledge_grants.summary: Dunmere's fear is making it easier to blame Garren and the road than to keep following evidence.
